expected_claims.text: Selected reimbursement support now justifies expansion for targeted behavioral-health and some chronic-care follow-up services, but parity is not universal.
Compliance constraints require state-clustered rollout rather than uniform multistate expansion.
Access benefits are strongest for behavioral-health follow-up and rural or mobility-limited patients.
Cost and utilization uncertainty still require triage and utilization controls, especially for chronic-care follow-up.

The recommendation should prioritize behavioral-health follow-up and rural or mobility-limited segments while keeping chronic-care expansion more cautious, payer-validated, compliance-gated, and state-clustered.
